body: These might be redundant for GCC, the `_COLD_` flags on `main.h` should be enough to propagate to `initialize_modules` and thus each module's initialization. This comes from an earlier attempt at trying to get similar gains on Clang by being more explicit. I'll do some more tests and remove the ones which aren't necessary for GCC and didn't have much benefit for Clang either.

body:
Ah, right.
I always assumed an atomic would cost on access, though I never actually checked if it's true.
But the initializer has a dual-entry guard with the mutex, so even if the variable is out of date on access, nothing bad happens.

`inline` is implied by `template` so it's not needed.
Don't feel strongly on this though so feel free to keep it if you prefer.

```suggestion
template <void (*A)(), void (*B)()>
constexpr bool _is_same_function = false;
template <void (*A)()>
constexpr bool _is_same_function<A, A> = true;
```
I'm happy either way, I can do that change next time I need to push an update (it's `object.h` so would be a full CI build).
